subject.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics

question: Should OpenClaw accept this trusted inbound contract as top-level bareBody/inboundDecorated fields on persisted/runtime user messages, or require it under OpenClaw-owned metadata before merge?
rationale: The code path is the right class of fix, but the field location becomes a durable session-message and reader trust contract with compatibility and security-boundary impact that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Accept current top-level contract
options.body: Merge this shape after exact-head real setup proof, accepting the two fields as additive message-level contract surface.

options.title: Move under OpenClaw metadata
options.body: Require a rework to store the trusted decoration under an OpenClaw-owned metadata object before merge, reducing generic message-schema exposure.

options.title: Pause for contract design
options.body: Hold this PR until maintainers settle the canonical inbound-decoration message contract on the linked issue.

recommendation.title: Accept current top-level contract
recommendation.body: Merge this shape after exact-head real setup proof, accepting the two fields as additive message-level contract surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing signal is recent history on inbound metadata plus the cross-session/runtime nature of this trust-boundary decision.
